The first floor is the reception area and the dog-related sales area.
The second floor is the cat-related sales area.
The third floor is a cat cafe where you can interact with several cats 🐈 (holding them is prohibited ❌️).
The fourth floor is a rabbit cafe 🐇 (holding them is also prohibited ❌️).
Free drinks (bottled water, black tea, green tea, etc.) are available on the third floor 🥤.

I recently visited this pet shop and witnessed a disturbing incident.

Immediately to the right upon entering the store, on the second level of a cage, a staff member opened the door to clean the litter box, causing a Chihuahua-Dachshund mix puppy inside to fall onto the floor on its back.

The puppy was crying out in pain, but the staff member didn't seem particularly flustered, and their attempts to catch the puppy as it fell seemed insufficient.

It's entirely predictable that a puppy would try to escape if the door is opened, so precautions and measures to prevent falls are necessary. Dachshunds, in particular, are prone to back strain, and this is especially true for very young puppies.

Furthermore, the store had a very strong odor, raising concerns about hygiene management. Because animals spend long hours in this space, thorough cleaning and ventilation, as well as other daily management practices, are essential.

I hope the puppy that fell receives necessary examinations and monitoring to ensure it is not injured. Furthermore, to prevent the same thing from happening again, I would like you to thoroughly implement safety measures, staff training, and management of the store environment.

DO NOT VISIT this cat cafe.  This place is filthy, unsanitary, inhumane and should be shut down.  It’s a disgrace to Japan.

As soon as you walked in, you’re welcomed with the smell of cat pee.  There was no litter box, food or water in sight.  The room temperature was 28C!  The temperature was literally cooler outside.  All of the cats seemed to be miserable and sad.  They were not playful at all.  The drinks (included with ticket) in the fridge were room temperature.  When looking around, the place was filled with mold and dust.  We felt terrible for the cats.

Bad smell when i walked inside the shop, the puppies and kittens were kept in small glass boxes under very bright lights. Some puppies looked sick and were sneezing. This store is disgusting and cruel to animals, I originally wanted to visit the cat cafe but couldn’t after the smell and the bad conditions of the animals.
Very dirty and more of a cat hostel than rather than a cafe...
I highly discourage any customers from this place. The dogs kept for sale are under horrible conditions.

This place is a disgrace to Japan, the puppies were kept in glass tanks alone, 24 hrs, looking depressed. Puppies which were even very young all day locked in a wall exposition under neon lights, some of them looking dehydrated and unwell. This made me feel really sad and I believe it's a way to make customers feel sorry for the dog and then buy it. The consumeristic approach promoted by the store goes against all animal welfare and exposes a big weakness with regards to ethics upheld by this business.

The cat and rabbit cafes are actually rooms where attendees can help themselves to drinks in the freezer and play with the animals. When we arrived, there weren't any cat toys available which I think staff forgot to put out hence why I docked 1 star but we overall had a good experience!

We were sent there from the other cat café, Mocha Lounge (since my daughter is under 13). The staff seemed annoyed by the two of us. The lounge, where you're with the cats, smelled bad. The cats couldn't retreat and seemed stressed. I can't recommend it. We went to Harajuku afterwards, and it was much friendlier, cleaner, and more child-friendly!
